\par\medskip\noindent\textbf{Supplementary Note 9. Label transfer.}\par\smallskip
\begingroup\small\setlength{\parskip}{3pt}
\noindent\textit{Embeddings.} Label transfer asks whether a batch's cell types can be predicted from the other batches in the latent space. For each penalty, task and decoder it is read on the embeddings (posterior means) of the matched strength, the strength with no failed fit whose seed-mean batch score is nearest $b^*$, ties to the smaller strength, edge and extension strengths included (Supplementary Note 5), with its three sweep seeds (100--102). The strength is chosen from batch scores only, never by label-transfer accuracy. Plain scVI (three seeds, each decoder) and the scvi-tools adversarial classifier (five seeds, 0--4, batch-conditioned decoder only) have no strength to choose and are shown unmatched. Harmony, Scanorama, sysVI, scANVI and PCA are not label-transferred.

\noindent\textit{Classifier and score.} Cell types present in only one batch of a task are dropped, a choice made from the labels alone. Each remaining batch is held out in turn, and its cells' types are predicted from the cells of the other batches by a 15-nearest-neighbour classifier (scikit-learn's k-nearest-neighbour classifier with Euclidean distance and equal vote weights). The score of a held-out batch is the macro F1, the F1 per cell type averaged over the cell types present in that batch; the score of an embedding is the mean over its held-out batches, and the table gives the mean and standard deviation over seeds. Every one of the 120 method, task and decoder entries could be scored (no task lost all its cell types).

\noindent\textit{Distance to $b^*$.} Matched strengths are fitted strengths, so their batch scores are near $b^*$ but not on it. Beside each value the table gives the seed-mean batch score of the embeddings and its distance from $b^*$; for plain scVI and the scvi-tools adversary, the distance of their own batch score. Distances differ between penalties, and a penalty read further above $b^*$ has removed more batch effect, which can lower its label-transfer score; values should be compared with the distances in view.

\noindent\textit{Summary and scope.} For each method and decoder, the cross-task summary is the mean macro F1 over the real tasks that are not low-signal (five with the batch-conditioned decoder, six with the unconditioned decoder). Low-signal pairs are tabulated and marked but not summarised; simulations are tabulated and not averaged with the real tasks. No test or contrast between methods is computed. The analysis also scored label transfer on every sweep embedding (3,073 embeddings, the penalties at every fitted strength, plain scVI and the scvi-tools adversary), giving each penalty a label-transfer curve over strength (\texttt{label\_transfer\_curve.csv} of the sweep analysis); the matched-strength values below are read from those results and are the ones reported. F1 per cell type is in Supplementary Figure S3, and the per-type recall and confusion of the direct biology check in Supplementary Note 12.
